thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime p99 spike detected on hosted-api-prod (eu-west-1). p95->p99 gap widened, streaming stalls flagged by detector. Auto-page sent to oncall.
jamie: Oncall (jamie) here, acknowledging. :eyes: starting quick triage.
jamie: Can someone grab grafana links / top queries?
priya: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streams/realtime?orgId=1&from=now-30m
priya: quick look — p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s at 08:22 UTC, error rate small but tail latency for streaming endpoints spiked. KV cache hit rate dropped ~35% in eu-west-1.
leo: seeing same in runtime logs, a subset of workers reporting repeated stall logs: `WARN worker: stream stall detected, stall_duration_ms=1200`
jamie: initial mitigation idea: temporary route-shift for eu-west traffic to eu-central fallback pool, and enable deduced burst-capacity. Anyone object?
marta: support: two paying customers reported slow responses in the last 20m, some timeouts on streaming sessions. I'll open customer tickets once we confirm mitigation.
priya: no objections. I'm going to run quick KV cache metrics and check prefix cache eviction counts.
priya: running query: `select count(*) from kv_cache_evictions where region='eu-west-1' and ts > now()-30m`
priya: result: eviction spike ~ +420 evictions starting 08:20 UTC. That aligns with the tail spike. :thumbsup:
leo: suspecting a bad model variant rollout earlier today that increased memory pressure on workers. Checking rollout history...
leo: rollout: model-serving/v2.4.1 -> v2.4.2 at 05:00 UTC (canary then gradual). Backend logs show v2.4.2 workers using ~15% more mem.
jamie: ok. Two-part plan: 1) short route-shift eu-west -> eu-central for streaming endpoints only, 2) rollback or scale up eu-west model workers (prefer rollback if safe). Priya, can you coordinate route-shift?
priya: doing route-shift now. CLI: `infra route set --from=eu-west-1 --to=eu-central-1 --service=streaming --weight=0.0 --dry-run=false`
incident-bot: ACTION: route-shift executed by priya at 08:29 UTC. Traffic to eu-west streaming endpoints redirected to eu-central fallback pool.
jamie: enabling burst capacity for eu-west just in case: `infra capacity adjust --region=eu-west-1 --pool=dedicated --burst=on`
sre-bot: NOTE: Burst capacity increase requested by jamie queued. Estimated provision time ~90s.
leo: starting rollback of v2.4.2 on a small subset (canary rollback) to validate. Command: `svc deploy rollback model-serving v2.4.1 --region=eu-west-1 --count=4`
leo: canary rollback in progress. Monitoring logs.
priya: post-shift metrics: p99 for streaming in eu-west dropped from 1.8s -> 320ms within 60s of route-shift. p95 back to ~200ms.
marta: updating support: telling affected customers we mitigated, currently watching for recurrence.
jamie: customer impact estimate: ~0.4% of requests saw >1s latency, ~12k sessions touched in last 30m, two customers reported timeouts — flagged for follow-up.
leo: canary rollback looks clean; no error increase. Proceeding to roll forward rollback to remaining workers.
leo: full rollback complete at 08:39 UTC. Observability shows memory usage back to normal.
priya: KV cache hit rate recovering, evictions trending down.
jamie: great. Keep watch for 30m. Priya/Leo to own until next handoff, Marta to continue customer comms.
marta: noted, I'll send customer summary and follow-up timeline.
priya: adding a short alert rule tweak: increase detector sensitivity threshold to reduce noise from transient spikes; will submit PR for review.
jamie: handing off active watch to priya. I'm signing off from oncall for now — will monitor quietly. Handoff at 08:50 UTC. :white_check_mark:
priya: taking handoff. I'll keep the incident thread updated every 10m or on material changes.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: status -> mitigated (route-shift + rollback). Duration so far: ~28m.
jamie: closing initial triage. If anything recurs, reopen paging. Thanks all. :pray:
